description: Aristotle claims whose truth is settled by modern zoology, used as an answer key for assessor truth scores. verdict is the modern verdict on the claim as stated (universal claims fail on important exceptions; compound claims fail if any part fails). group: vindicated = true but doubted or dismissed for centuries before being confirmed; confirmed = true and not seriously disputed; refuted = false. settled is the year the question was settled, where one event settled it. blind_statement replaces the statement in the blind condition when the original names a period source. revised records a verdict changed after reviewing assessor disagreements; exclude marks a claim left out of scoring because its verdict depends on an uncertain identification or reading.

claims.evidence: Mustelus mustelus has a yolk-sac placenta joining embryo and uterus; dismissed as fable until Müller re-examined specimens.
claims.source: Müller J. 1842. Über den glatten Hai des Aristoteles. Abh. Königl. Akad. Wiss. Berlin.

claims.evidence: Placental viviparity, with the embryo nourished through a uterine connection after the yolk is spent, occurs in several shark families (Mustelus, Carcharhinus, Sphyrna).
claims.source: Müller J. 1842 (as above); Hamlett WC (ed.) 2005. Reproductive Biology and Phylogeny of Chondrichthyes.

claims.evidence: Male paternal care of nest and fry in the Acheloos catfish, doubted until Agassiz identified the species and named it Glanis (now Silurus) aristotelis; the 40-50 day figure is approximate.
claims.source: Agassiz L. 1857, naming Glanis aristotelis; Kottelat M, Freyhof J. 2007. Handbook of European Freshwater Fishes.

claims.evidence: The channa (Serranus cabrilla) is a simultaneous hermaphrodite and the erythrinus (Pagellus erythrinus) a protogynous hermaphrodite, so specimens carry ovarian tissue; males as separate fish do not exist in the first.
claims.source: Standard ichthyology; FishBase species accounts for Serranus cabrilla and Pagellus erythrinus.
claims.exclude: The erythrinus is usually identified as Pagellus erythrinus, a protogynous hermaphrodite whose larger fish are male, so the claim fails for it unless the identification is wrong; the channa part holds.

claims.evidence: Spotted hyenas are not hermaphrodites, contrary to a belief that persisted into the early modern period; both sexes have a subcaudal anal scent pouch.
claims.source: Frank LG. 1997. Evolution of genital masculinization: why do female hyaenas have such a large 'penis'? Trends Ecol Evol 12:58-62.

claims.evidence: Pangenesis (gemmules drawn from every part of the body) was revived by Darwin in 1868 and refuted by Galton's transfusion experiments and Weismann's germ-plasm theory.
claims.source: Galton F. 1871. Proc R Soc Lond 19:393-410; Weismann A. 1892. Das Keimplasma.

claims.evidence: Epigenesis: organs form in succession, as against preformationism, which dominated the 17th-18th centuries until Wolff and von Baer.
claims.source: Wolff CF. 1759. Theoria generationis; von Baer KE. 1828. Über Entwickelungsgeschichte der Thiere.

claims.evidence: Traits can skip a generation and reappear in grandchildren (recessive inheritance), explained by Mendelian genetics.
claims.source: Mendel G. 1866. Versuche über Pflanzen-Hybriden; rediscovered 1900.

claims.evidence: The hive leader is the mother of the colony's queens and workers; Aristotle's 'king' is the queen, whose sex and role were established by dissection.
claims.source: Butler C. 1609. The Feminine Monarchie; Swammerdam J., Biblia Naturae (1737, from 1670s dissections).

claims.evidence: Caprification: fig wasps (Blastophaga psenes) emerging from caprifigs pollinate Smyrna-type figs, which otherwise drop unripe; the mechanism was worked out in the 19th century.
claims.source: Standard pomology and fig-wasp mutualism literature.

claims.evidence: Anglerfishes (Lophius) lure prey with the illicium and esca while lying camouflaged on the bottom.
Spider-hunting wasps (Sceliphron, Trypoxylon, many Pompilidae) paralyse spiders, seal them in mud cells and lay eggs on them.
Distraction (broken-wing) displays by ground-nesting birds including partridges are well documented.
The common cuckoo is an obligate brood parasite that removes a host egg and lays one egg per host nest in nests of smaller birds.
claims.source: Davies NB. 2000. Cuckoos, Cowbirds and Other Cheats.

claims.evidence: Torpedo rays stun prey with electric discharges strong enough to numb humans.
Octopuses change colour and pattern to match the substrate when hunting and when alarmed.
claims.source: Hanlon RT, Messenger JB. 2018. Cephalopod Behaviour, 2nd ed.

claims.evidence: Female Octopus vulgaris brood their eggs, stop feeding and decline (semelparous senescence).
Only male cicadas have tymbals and sing.
Dolphins are viviparous with two mammary glands in slits beside the genital slit.
All cetaceans are viviparous placental mammals.
Horned ruminants lack upper incisors and have a four-chambered stomach and chew the cud.
Brown bear females give birth in the winter den in January-February, fast throughout, and emerge with cubs in spring.
Elephant gestation is about 22 months and births are almost always single.
Canine gestation is about 63 days (58-68 from mating); markedly premature litters do not survive.
Elephants swim and wade using the trunk as a snorkel.
claims.source: West JB. 2002. Why doesn't the elephant have a pleural space? News Physiol Sci 17:47-50.

claims.evidence: A worker honeybee stinging a vertebrate leaves the barbed sting with venom sac and part of the abdomen, and dies.

claims.blind_statement: Human semen is white in every population; it is not black in any human population.
claims.evidence: Semen colour does not vary with skin pigmentation.
In the chick embryo the heart begins beating around day 2 as a red point, with the vitelline vessels leading from it.
The heart is the first functional organ to form in vertebrate embryos.
claims.revised: Verdict changed from true after review of assessor rationales (2026-10-31): Compound: the heart is the first organ to form, but it is not the origin of the other parts.

claims.evidence: Dogs, wolves, foxes, jackals and lions are born with fused eyelids that open days to weeks after birth.
claims.revised: Verdict changed from true after review of assessor rationales (2026-10-31): Universal over many-toed quadrupeds: spotted hyenas are born with open eyes and many-toed rodents such as guinea pigs are precocial.

claims.evidence: Pupae of holometabolous insects do not feed or defecate; wastes are voided as meconium at eclosion.
Decapod crustaceans moult repeatedly through life and are soft after each moult.
Rock pigeons are socially monogamous long-term with occasional extra-pair copulation.
Cuckoos are not transformed hawks; the resemblance is hawk mimicry in plumage.
Hens and geese lay unfertilised eggs without ever mating.
Grey mullets enter estuaries and fresh water; European eels are catadromous and migrate down to the sea to spawn.
Common and demoiselle cranes breeding on the Eurasian steppes winter in Sudan and Ethiopia.
Litter or clutch size falls with body size across animals as a strong tendency.
Paired horns occur only in artiodactyls; no perissodactyl has paired horns (rhino horns are median keratin).
Female-biased sexual size dimorphism is the norm in most insect taxa.
Female sharks and rays are usually larger than males, as are females in most fishes.
Male chondrichthyans have paired claspers on the pelvic fins.
Elasmobranchs have open gill slits without an operculum.
claims.revised: Verdict changed from true after review of assessor rationales (2026-10-31): Compound: selachians lack opercula, but cartilage is not the cause; chimaeras are cartilaginous and have an opercular flap.

claims.evidence: Most fish eggs and larvae die before maturity; high fecundity offsets this mortality.
In temperate Vespula and Vespa, workers die in autumn and only mated queens overwinter in sheltered holes.
Honeybee workers tear down queen cells when no swarm is to issue and kill supernumerary queens.
claims.source: Winston ML. 1987. The Biology of the Honey Bee.
claims.exclude: Workers do destroy surplus queen cells, but rival queens do much of the killing, so whether workers kill most queens is disputed.

claims.evidence: Mediterranean snakes, lizards and geckos brumate for several winter months without feeding.
claims.revised: Verdict changed from true after review of assessor rationales (2026-10-31): The claim includes the river crocodile, which does not hide or fast for four winter months; the snake and lizard part holds for temperate species.

claims.evidence: Eagle pairs defend large territories and young disperse from the natal territory.
claims.exclude: Eagles defend territories and young disperse, but other bird species do settle near eagle nests, so the verdict depends on how broadly the last clause is read.

claims.evidence: Nile crocodiles bask by day and return to water at night, which then holds heat better than the air.
claims.source: Cott HB. 1961. Trans Zool Soc Lond 29:211-356.

claims.evidence: Honeybees show flower constancy, keeping to one species on a foraging trip.
claims.source: Grant V. 1950. Bot Rev 16:379-398; Free JB. 1963. J Anim Ecol 32:119-131.

claims.evidence: Men castrated before puberty do not develop androgenic hair or a deepened voice and do not develop male-pattern baldness.
Capons lose comb colour, crowing and sexual behaviour; caponised young cocks never develop them.
claims.source: Berthold AA. 1849. Transplantation der Hoden. Arch Anat Physiol Wiss Med.

claims.evidence: Mutilations are not inherited.
The hectocotylus transfers spermatophores into the female's mantle cavity; it is the male's copulatory organ, not merely a holdfast.
claims.source: Steenstrup J. 1856, on hectocotylus formation; Hanlon RT, Messenger JB. 2018.

claims.evidence: Argonauts do not sail; the webbed dorsal arms secrete and hold the shell, as Villepreux-Power showed in aquarium observations in the 1830s.
claims.source: Finn JK, Norman MD. 2010. Proc R Soc B 277:2967-2971.

claims.evidence: There is no reliable observation of any bird cleaning the teeth of crocodiles.
Swallows, kites, storks, turtle-doves and larks migrate or overwinter active; bird ringing showed swallows winter in Africa.
Eels have gonads (ovaries found 1777, testes 1874) and spawn in the Sargasso Sea; gonads stay undeveloped in fresh water, which is why none were seen.
claims.source: Schmidt J. 1922. The breeding places of the eel. Phil Trans R Soc B 211:179-208.

claims.evidence: Eels hatch from eggs spawned at sea and arrive as leptocephali and glass eels; they do not arise from earthworms.
Molluscs, barnacles and ascidians develop from fertilised eggs via planktonic larvae; spontaneous generation was refuted.
Honeybees do not carry stones as ballast.
Bees make honey by enzymatically processing and dehydrating nectar (or insect honeydew); honey does not fall from the air, and wax is secreted by glands, not made from flowers.
Dental formulae do not differ between the sexes in humans, sheep, goats or pigs (canine size may differ, not number).
Cranial suture patterns do not differ between the sexes.
Humans normally have twelve pairs of ribs.
Lions have seven cervical vertebrae, like nearly all mammals.
In humans the right kidney lies lower than the left (in many quadrupeds it is more cranial), so the universal claim fails.
The brain is densely vascularised and receives about 15% of cardiac output.
Sensation depends on the brain, as Herophilus and Galen showed experimentally; the heart is not the sensory centre.
Fishes have inner ears with otoliths, lateral lines and olfactory organs with external nares.
Epizootics are common in fishes (viral haemorrhagic septicaemia, koi herpesvirus, infectious salmon anaemia).
Skates, chimaeras and catsharks lay egg cases, so not all cartilaginous fishes are viviparous; the fishing-frog (Lophius) is a bony fish.
Great apes laugh when tickled, and rats emit ultrasonic calls when tickled.
claims.source: Davila Ross M, Owren MJ, Zimmermann E. 2009. Curr Biol 19:1106-1111; Panksepp J, Burgdorf J. 2003. Physiol Behav 79:533-547.

claims.evidence: Most newborns worldwide have brown eyes; only some, mainly of European ancestry, are born with blue-grey eyes that may darken.
Hair and nails do not grow after death; skin retraction from dehydration makes them appear longer.
Bowhead whales, giant tortoises and Greenland sharks outlive humans, and elephants do not.
claims.source: Nielsen J et al. 2016. Science 353:702-704; George JC et al. 1999. Can J Zool 77:571-580.

claims.evidence: Naturally conceived sextuplets are documented, and larger multiple births occur with fertility treatment.
Many interspecific hybrids besides mules are sterile or male-sterile (hinnies, zebroids, ligers' males; Haldane's rule).
Crocodiles open the mouth by moving the lower jaw; the upper jaw is fused to the skull.
Claw handedness in decapods is often random or 50:50 (fiddler crabs, many lobsters), so the right claw is not invariably larger.
Squid and cuttlefish have eight arms plus two tentacles, and nautiluses have about ninety appendages.
Egg shape does not predict chick sex.
Acquired marks such as scars are not inherited; only some congenital conditions are heritable.
Scorpion young ride on the mother's back and do not kill her; matriphagy occurs only in a few spiders.
Donkeys have their own sucking louse (Haematopinus asini) and carry ticks.
Clinical rabies is almost always fatal in humans too.
Swans have no death song; the 'swan song' is legend.
Birds require copulation for fertilisation; partridges are not impregnated by wind or voice.
The common kingfisher breeds in spring and summer, not at the winter solstice.
Greying with age is common in dogs, chimpanzees and other mammals.
By brain-to-body mass ratio shrews, small rodents and some small birds exceed humans (humans lead only on encephalization quotient).
Boys are fertile from mid-adolescence, not about 21.
Sessile animals such as oysters, mussels and barnacles produce eggs and sperm, as separate sexes or hermaphrodites.
Many motile animals are hermaphrodites (earthworms, most land snails, flatworms).
Monotremes, including the spiny echidna, have hair and lay eggs.
claims.source: Caldwell WH. 1884, telegram 'Monotremes oviparous, ovum meroblastic'.

claims.evidence: Viviparous sharks, guppies and eelpouts breathe water through gills.
Vultures, kites and some hawks (Harris's hawk, Swainson's hawk) live, roost or hunt in groups.
Muntjacs and tufted deer have both tusk-like canines and antlers.
Honeybee age polyethism runs the other way: young workers work inside the hive, older ones forage, and foragers become worn and hairless.
In nearly all insects the male inserts the aedeagus into the female; the reverse is known only in rare cases such as Neotrogla.
claims.source: Yoshizawa K et al. 2014. Curr Biol 24:1006-1010.

claims.evidence: Cetaceans are usually born tail first, so birth is not head first in all animals.
Most small birds, including most passerines, breed in the season after hatching, within their first year.
